note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a BRU 8; A06b BRU 8; L05 BRU 9(5)(a)): ordinary naturalisation after 20 years' residence; no renunciation of other citizenships required; a citizen loses the citizenship on voluntarily taking another. Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Group restriction: only if citizen parent is member of a particular group, race or religion), A01b (descent, born abroad: Group restriction: only if citizen parent is member of a particular group, race or religion), A02a (birth in country: Group restriction: only if parent is member of a particular group, race or religion) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: Group restriction: only if parent is member of a particular group, race or religion), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: by birth in the territory only on the condition the dataset states; by descent from the father only, a child born abroad on the limit the dataset states. The coding also records a restriction to members of a particular group, which the form holds only in the condition's words, which the form doesn't hold. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file.

sources.title: GLOBALCIT Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (Vink, van der Baaren, Bauböck, Dzankic, Honohan, Manby; EUI Research Data, 2025), country-year-mode files, Brunei, 2024
sources.said: Person has been lawfully resident in Brunei for at least 20 years in the aggregate within a period of 25 years immediately prior to the application, as well as throughout the 2 years immediately prior to the application. Intent to settle permanently in the country required. ... n.a. ... Person voluntarily acquires citizenship of another country. ... Group restriction: only if citizen parent is member of a particular group, race or religion ... Person is born in Brunei to a father who is a citizen. ... Group restriction: only if citizen parent is member of a particular group, race or religion ... Person is born abroad to a father who (1) was born in Brunei and belongs to one of the specified indigenous groups of the Malay race and (2) is employed abroad in the service of the Brunei government or a Brunei company. Or person is born to a father who was born abroad and who in turn was born to a father who was born in Brunei and belongs to one of the specified indigenous groups of the Malay race. Child needs to be registered within 6 months after birth.; Person is born abroad to a father who (1) was born in Brunei to a mother and father who were both born in Brunei and are members of any of the groups of people specified in the 1st Schedule (i.e. people who are indigenous to Brunei, but note that the list is longer than the indigenous people referred to under BRU 4(1)a) and (2) is employed abroad in the service of the Brunei government or a Brunei company. Or person is born abroad to a father and mother who were both born in Brunei and are members of any of the groups specified in the 1st Schedule. Child needs to be registered within 6 months after birth.; Person is born abroad to a father who is a citizen and is employed abroad in the service of the Brunei government or a Brunei company. Child needs to be registered within 6 months after birth.; Person is born abroad to a father who is a citizen by registration or naturalisation. Child needs to be registered within 6 months after birth. ... Group restriction: only if parent is member of a particular group, race or religion ... Person is born in Brunei and belongs to one of the specified indigenous groups of the Malay race. ... Group restriction: only if parent is member of a particular group, race or religion ... Person is born in Brunei to a father and mother who were both born in Brunei and are members of any of the groups of people specified in the 1st Schedule (i.e. people who are indigenous to Brunei, but note that the list is longer than the indigenous people referred to under BRU 4(1)a).
